title: Linux Processes, Threads, UIDs, and the App Sandbox Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies linux processes, threads, uids, and the app sandbox?
options: Model PID as ephemeral execution, UID as security identity, threads as shared-memory execution, and persist state needed after process death.
questions.answer: Model PID as ephemeral execution, UID as security identity, threads as shared-memory execution, and persist state needed after process death.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: Every Android component declared by one package always runs in the same Linux process.
questions.explanation: Treating the Application singleton as durable global state loses data and invariants whenever Android kills and later recreates the process.

questions.prompt: What is the security-relevant distinction between UID and PID?
questions.answer: The UID identifies the app sandbox and permissions, while a PID identifies one temporary running process instance.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
